# 04 Fine magnetite concentration

> How fine must magnetite be ground to reach a pellet-feed grade?

A magnetite ore ground in closed circuit and upgraded by low-intensity magnetic drums; magnetite is recovered even in composites, so concentrate iron grade follows liberation and therefore the grind.

| Case id | Category | Circuit family | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iron_magnetite_fine` | liberation | magnetic | authored scenario; parameters inside cited ranges; not plant-calibrated |

Open it in the workbench: [https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=iron_magnetite_fine](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=iron_magnetite_fine); on its own stage: [focus](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/focus/iron_magnetite_fine).

## The problem

The drums work at 800 to 2000 G and lose little beyond the ultrafine magnetite, so the concentrate grade pays for the silica that composites carry into it.

At Zandrivierspoort a 35.7% Fe feed gave 64.9% Fe at 80% passing 75 µm and 69.0% Fe at 80% passing 45 µm, with rougher magnetite recovery above 98%. The case asks how fine the ore must be ground for a pellet-feed grade.

## The ore

| Mineral | Role | Mass fraction | Liberation size | Composite content | Host | Separation response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Magnetite | Fe carrier (stoichiometric) | from the head grade | 130 µm | 0.50 | Iron-bearing silicate gangue | magnetic field |
| Iron-bearing silicate gangue | gangue | the balance | - | - | - | - |

| Payable | Head grade | Carried by |
|---|---|---|
| Fe | 26.5% | Magnetite (100%, stoichiometric) |

Bond ball-mill work index 13.5 kWh/t; crushing work index 15.0 kWh/t.

## The plant

| Unit | Declared |
|---|---|
| Crusher | Whiten crusher; feed F80 60 mm |
| Ball mill | 20,300 kW installed; discharge at 72% solids |
| Cyclones | 25.4 cm diameter, sharpness 2.0; 62 required at the nominal state |
| Magnetic drums | rougher and cleaner LIMS; up to 99.5% capture of liberated magnetite |
| Grade specification | Fe at least 65.0% |
| Process water | at most 2.52 m³ per tonne |

The nominal state and the bounds Contract 1 allows for this case; the workbench validates every change against them.

| Input | Nominal | Allowed range |

| Ore throughput | 920 t/h | 460 t/h to 1,380 t/h |
| Grind target (P80) | 60.0 µm | 30.0 µm to 120.0 µm |
| Circulating load | 2.50 | 1.00 to 4.00 |
| Overflow water | 2.40 m³/t | 1.00 m³/t to 4.00 m³/t |
| Crusher closed-side setting | 8.00 mm | 4.00 mm to 16.00 mm |
| Bond work index | 13.5 kWh/t | 9.5 kWh/t to 20.3 kWh/t |
| Head grade | 26.5% | 13.3% to 39.8% |

## The six variants

Each variant changes exactly one input of the nominal state.

| Variant | Change | Recovery of the primary payable | Concentrate grade | Specific energy, total | Product P80 | Mill power | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal design | - | 84.9% | 65.74% | 20.75 kWh/t | 60 µm | 18,147 kW | - |
| Harder ore (+25% work index) | Bond work index: 13.5 kWh/t to 16.9 kWh/t (x1.25) | 85.5% | 64.28% | 23.34 kWh/t | 71 µm | 20,300 kW | `power_limited` |
| Coarser grind target (+35% P80) | Grind target (P80): 60.0 µm to 81.0 µm (x1.35) | 85.9% | 63.07% | 17.26 kWh/t | 81 µm | 14,935 kW | - |
| Finer grind target (-25% P80) | Grind target (P80): 60.0 µm to 45.0 µm (x0.75) | 84.3% | 67.05% | 23.09 kWh/t | 51 µm | 20,300 kW | `power_limited`, `cyclone_pressure` |
| Higher throughput (+25%) | Ore throughput: 920 t/h to 1,150 t/h (x1.25) | 85.5% | 64.28% | 18.68 kWh/t | 71 µm | 20,300 kW | `power_limited` |
| Finer crusher setting (-20% CSS) | Crusher closed-side setting: 8.00 mm to 6.40 mm (x0.80) | 84.9% | 65.74% | 20.57 kWh/t | 60 µm | 17,808 kW | - |

- **Harder ore (+25% work index).** Bond work index 25% higher. The circuit needs more energy per tonne for the same grind; where the installed power runs out the mill runs at its limit and the product coarsens, which then costs liberation.
- **Coarser grind target (+35% P80).** Grind target 35% coarser. Less energy per tonne and fewer liberated grains, so the concentrate grade falls; a flotation circuit pays for the energy saved in recovery as well, while magnetic drums keep capturing the coarser composites and recover a little more iron at the lower grade.
- **Finer grind target (-25% P80).** Grind target 25% finer. More of the valuable mineral is liberated from its host, so a concentrate that depends on liberation gains grade, at a higher specific energy.
- **Higher throughput (+25%).** Throughput 25% higher. Once the mill reaches its installed power the grind coarsens, and in a flotation circuit the residence in every bank falls in proportion as well; the metal recovered per hour can still rise, because the extra tonnes outweigh the recovery lost.
- **Finer crusher setting (-20% CSS).** Crusher closed-side setting 20% tighter. The mill receives a finer feed, so the same grind target needs less grinding energy per tonne.

## At the nominal state

| Check | Value | Plausible range | Within |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recovery of the primary payable | 84.9% | 70.0% to 92.0% | yes |
| Concentrate grade | 65.74% | 63.00% to 70.00% | yes |
| magnetite recovery pct | 94.38% | 90.00% to 99.50% | yes |

Every unit and the circuit close within 5.8e-16 relative (the requirement is 1e-9). Water: 2.40 m³/t.

## Method records at the nominal state

- **Optimizer:** optimal at Grind target (P80) 65.6 µm; active constraint: grade; recovered metal +0.35% against the nominal state (20 engine runs from 4 starts).
- **Uncertainty** (128 Latin-hypercube samples of the ore): recovery P05 81.9%, P50 85.0%, P95 87.3%; probability of meeting every constraint 55%.
- **Sobol indices** (1280 engine runs), the input with the largest total index: recovery of the primary payable: head grade (total index 0.99); concentrate grade: liberation size (total index 0.97); specific energy, grinding: work index (total index 1.00); recovered primary payable: head grade (total index 1.00).
- **Kinetic fits:** not applicable (no flotation).

## Scope and assumptions

There is no flotation: the rougher and cleaner drums capture by particle class, with ultrafine losses and gangue entrapment.

The published grind-grade pairs are the oracle for the direction and size of the effect, not a calibration of this plant.

## Reading it in the workbench

Separation: the LIMS capture curves by particle class show why composites lower the grade.

Case, variants and cases: the finer-grind and coarser-grind variants bracket the nominal grade.

- **breakage:** Moly-Cop Tools energy-specific selection (alpha0 0.0091 t/kWh, alpha1 0.651, alpha2 2.5, d_crit 6514 µm) and its documented alternative breakage set (beta0 0.4, beta1 0.65, beta2 4.02); dossier section 1.4.

- **cyclone:** Plitt geometry ratios typical of mineral-processing cyclones; sharpness and underflow density authored; dossier section 2.
- **magnetic:** LIMS magnetite recovery above 98% and grade rising with finer grind (Muthaphuli 2014); dossier section 5.
- **water:** Process-water capacity per tonne of ore (pumping and thickener capacity), authored 5% above each case's nominal requirement; it is the water constraint of the operating-point optimizer.
- **kpi:** Nominal KPI ranges are typical practice ranges from the dossier section 3.7 and the cited sources; they are plausibility gates, not predictions.
